key_insight: MicroSyn‑X generates realistic synthetic X‑ray data to train deep models that reliably track and enable real‑time robotic control of miniature medical devices, closing the sim‑to‑real gap without large clinical datasets.
problem_solved: Scarcity and annotation difficulty of high‑quality X‑ray images for tiny implantable devices make it hard to train and validate robust tracking and control models for surgical robotics.
method: Create a physics‑aware synthetic X‑ray generation pipeline with domain randomization to produce labeled, diverse training pairs that mimic clinical variability.
Train deep tracking/detection models on synthetic data and adapt to real X‑rays via sim‑to‑real techniques, then integrate models into a closed‑loop robotic navigation system for real‑time control.
Validate performance on challenging scenarios (occlusion, low contrast, motion) and demonstrate robust tracking and navigation in experimental setups.
impact: Enables rapid development and deployment of ML-driven tracking and autonomous control for miniature surgical devices without reliance on large annotated clinical datasets, accelerating research in surgical AI and safe robotic interventions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: synthetic X‑ray generation → labeled dataset → model training → robotic control loop
Side‑by‑side comparison of synthetic vs. real X‑ray frames with annotations to show realism and label fidelity
Performance chart: tracking accuracy / latency on synthetic‑trained vs. real‑trained models across occlusion and motion conditions
Sequence storyboard: robot navigates a miniature device in X‑ray frames showing closed‑loop corrections
paper_title: Synthetic X‑ray‑driven tracking and control of miniature medical devices
paper_authors: Chunxiang Wang, Wenbin Kang, Mengmeng Sun, Hongchuan Zhang, Chong Hong
